permitted_edits.purpose: Add the self-mining attacker (SB-S1): a private chain and an unpublished-block list, minting on the private tip, and the match/override/abandon rules applied when an honest block arrives; the attacker is the node whose id equals NUM_OF_NODES, the other nodes keep the original honest behaviour.
New minting task for the attacker: builds the block on the attacker's private tip and hands it to the attacker's private handler instead of adding it to the public chain and announcing it.

Give the attacker node the fixed hash rate 400000 and mark it as the self-mining attacker when the network is built, and print the ABC_METRIC lines for attacker_revenue_share and attacker_hash_share at the end of every run; the seed and plan-parameter lines the harness patches are kept unchanged.

question: In a 100-node SimBlock Bitcoin-like network, a single self-mining (block-withholding) attacker varies α from 0.10 to 0.40. How does its share of main-chain blocks compare with α, i.e. for which α is the attack profitable, and what happens to the orphan rate and to block propagation time (t90)?
rationale:
WHY SIMBLOCK. The attack works by making honest miners waste work on a branch that later loses, so the result depends on which chain individual honest nodes actually extend. SimBlock models that: a Bitcoin-like P2P network with per-node regions, bandwidth and latency (SB-M1), block propagation with compact block relay and churn nodes (SB-M2), PoW production with per-node mining power and difficulty tied to the target interval (SB-M3), and forks that arise naturally, with losing blocks recorded as orphans (SB-M4). Its node behaviour is the hook the attack needs (SB-S1), and a 100-node run is cheap (SB-C1). The paper this reproduces also used SimBlock ("We use SimBlock to simulate the blockchain network [8]").

WHY NOT BLOCKSIM. BlockSim collapses propagation into one exponential delay per block and has no network topology (BS-N2, BS-N1), so the fork and orphan structure the attack exploits is much coarser and there is no propagation-time metric; its Ethereum model (uncles), where "self-mining" in the literature is usually defined, is not offered by the harness (BS-N3). BlockSim's incentives and node0_block_share (BS-M4) would make revenue easier to measure, but at the cost of the network the question is about.

STRATEGY IMPLEMENTED (classic Eyal–Sirer selfish/self-mining withholding, γ = 0). The attacker is one node (id = NUM_OF_NODES) that mines on its private tip and does not announce what it finds. It reveals its whole private chain when the public chain catches up to the same height (match, a tie fork) or to one block behind (override, our chain is then strictly longer and wins); it abandons its private chain when the public chain becomes longer. SimBlock's fork choice accepts a block only if its total difficulty is strictly greater (ProofOfWork.isReceivedBlockValid), so honest nodes never switch on a tie: that is γ = 0, the case the validation value refers to. Blocks the attacker never publishes are simply not counted (nor recorded as orphans).

HOW α IS SET (disclosed assumption). The plan-parameter set has no attacker-hash-power name, so the attacker's hash rate is fixed in the edited code (400000, the card's upstream AVERAGE_MINING_POWER) and α is varied through the honest per-node hash rate AVERAGE_MINING_POWER with STDEV = 0: α = 400000 / (400000 + 99·AVERAGE_MINING_POWER). The realised α is printed as the metric attacker_hash_share; the requested values 0.10/0.20/0.25/0.30/0.33/0.40 come out to within 3e-4.

LIMITS. (1) SimBlock has no block rewards, fees or uncles (SB-N2), so "revenue" here is the attacker's share of main-chain blocks, not coins; the Ethereum uncle-reward form of self-mining cannot be measured. (2) The attacker is one node, not the 100α miners pooled in the paper. (3) The paper's attacker-favourable network (0 s for the attacker, 10 s between honest nodes) is not representable: region bandwidths and latencies are not plan parameters (SB-N3), so SimBlock's default regional latencies with CBR_USAGE_RATE 0.964 are used; CHURN_NODE_RATE is 0 so no node goes offline. (4) 1500 blocks per run instead of 100,000 (SB-C1); with 5 seeds the standard error of a revenue share near 0.5 is about 0.005, small next to the differences compared. (5) No difficulty adjustment within a run (SimBlock keeps nextDifficulty constant), so the block interval stays 600 s.
title: SimBlock self-mining attack: attacker revenue share vs hash power α

validation.description: Known-answer check on the withholding strategy itself, at γ = 0: for α = 0.4 the optimal withholding policy earns a revenue ratio of 0.48866 (Table 1 of arXiv:2007.05614, γ = 0 row α = 0.4). Honest mining would give 0.40, which is 0.089 away, so the check fails both if the attacker never withholds and if it withholds wrongly; 5 seeds of 1500 blocks give a standard error near 0.005, well inside the tolerance.
